recipes.title: Gemista
recipes.description: Sweet tomatoes and peppers filled with herby rice, baked until the kitchen smells like late summer in the village.
steps: Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers, hollow them out, and reserve the pulp from the tomatoes.
Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft, then add zucchini, chopped tomato pulp, tomato paste, rice, herbs, salt, and pepper.
Fill the vegetables three-quarters full with the rice mixture and place them in a baking dish with the potato wedges around them.
Drizzle generously with olive oil, add a splash of water, cover loosely with parchment, and bake until the vegetables collapse and caramelize.
Serve warm or at room temperature with feta and crusty bread.

memory.title: Grandma's pan on the balcony
memory.story: Every August, yiayia would line the tray on the balcony so the tomatoes could catch the last bit of sun before going into the oven. She always said the breeze from the sea made them sweeter, and we believed her because dinner always tasted like a holiday.

recipes.title: Spanakopita
recipes.description: A flaky spinach and feta pie wrapped in crisp phyllo, perfect for long kitchen conversations and second helpings.
ingredients: 1/2 cup olive oil or melted butter
Salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg
steps: Wilt the spinach in a pan, squeeze out excess liquid, and combine with spring onions, feta, eggs, herbs, and seasonings.
Brush a baking tin with olive oil and layer in half the phyllo sheets, brushing each sheet lightly.
Spread the spinach filling evenly, then cover with the remaining phyllo sheets, again brushing each layer.
Score the top into squares, sprinkle with a little water for extra crispness, and bake until deep golden.
Let the pie rest before cutting so the filling settles and the layers stay distinct.

memory.title: The wedding helper pie
memory.story: The night before my cousin's wedding, the kitchen table disappeared under stacks of phyllo and bowls of greens. Everyone had one job—brushing, folding, laughing—and the first baked tray vanished before midnight with mugs of mountain tea.

recipes.title: Chicken Avgolemono Soup
recipes.description: Silky lemony chicken soup that feels like a blanket on a rainy evening and somehow cures homesickness too.
ingredients: 1 whole chicken breast, cooked and shredded
steps: Cook carrot and celery in olive oil until softened, then add stock and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add rice or orzo and cook until tender, then stir in the shredded chicken.
Whisk eggs and lemon juice in a bowl until frothy.
Temper the egg mixture slowly with ladles of hot broth, whisking constantly.
Pour the avgolemono mixture back into the pot on very low heat, stirring gently until the soup turns silky. Do not boil.
Season and finish with dill before serving.

memory.title: A pot for stormy nights
memory.story: When winter rain knocked the power out, my mother would still find a way to keep a pot of avgolemono warm on the gas stove. We ate by candlelight, listening to the shutters rattle, and the bright lemony steam made the whole house feel safe.
